messages:
Alex: heads-up, after yesterday's kernel roll some services in the us-west-2 GPU pool are seeing intermittent DNS timeouts for intra-cluster calls, 5xx from our internal retries. :eyes:
Maria: OK, which resolver? node-local or coreDNS?
Alex: node-local (DaemonSet) + fallback to coreDNS. Timeouts look like: ~300-800ms spikes then normal for minutes.
Simon: I saw increased retries in the client side too, exponential backoff flooding later. Might be conntrack/backpressure.
infra-bot: alert: high_dns_retry_rate (metric: service.dns.retry_rate) triggered for cluster/gpu-uswest2 — 12% -> 48% over 10m
Jamie: can someone run tcpdump on a node with the issue? capture UDP 53 and conntrack stats.
Maria: doing quick check: pods on node-az-a-07 -> node-local svc 169.254.20.10:53 timing out. kubectl exec into test pod and running: 

```
# from test pod
dig @169.254.20.10 redis.internal.svc.cluster.local +time=2 +tries=2
; <<>> DiG 9.11.3 <<>> @169.254.20.10 redis.internal.svc.cluster.local +time=2 +tries=2
;; connection timed out; no servers could be reached
```

Maria: node-local logs show repeated "cache write failed: EAGAIN" and crashloop restart counts higher.
Alex: I also reproduced with curl -v to service name; looked like client resolved, then very slow connect because SRV A entries were delayed.
Simon: grabbed tcpdump: 
```
# tcpdump quick
18:12:10.123456 IP 10.0.3.12.54000 > 169.254.20.10.53: 12345 UDP, length 72
18:12:10.123789 IP 169.254.20.10.53 > 10.0.3.12.54000: 12345 UDP, length 88
# then many retransmits, some truncated fragments
```
Simon: also saw ICMP "frag needed" on a couple hosts after the kernel update. MTU might have changed on host egress.
Jamie: we rolled custom MTU clamp in 2 nodes for RDMA tests last week, could be related.
Alex: conntrack table on busy nodes ~95% full during spikes. Possibly the bursts of client retries (exponential) + node-local DNS using many ephemeral UDP sockets -> conntrack churn and NAT exhaustion.
Maria: run these checks if you're on a repro node: 
```
sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max
conntrack -S
iptables -vnL | grep DNAT
kubectl -n kube-system logs ds/node-local-dns -c node-cache --tail 200
tcpdump -i eth0 'udp port 53' -w /tmp/dns.pcap
```
Maria: I killed node-local on one repro node to force direct CoreDNS; timeouts dropped immediately for that node.
Simon: that suggests node-local proxy/backpressure is a big factor. But why did the kernel roll change behavior? Maybe different UDP buffer defaults or offload interactions with RDMA/MTU.
Jamie: rolling a small change: bump conntrack max on 2 nodes and disable ip_conntrack_tcp_timeout_established reduction we did earlier. Deploying now to canary nodes.
infra-bot: deploy started: conntrack-tuning to canary nodes (2/2) by Jamie at 18:20 UTC
Alex: after bumping conntrack on canary node we saw retry_rate drop from 47% -> 6% within 90s. Good signal.
Maria: follow-ups: 1) revert any MTU/RDMA experimental changes cluster-wide, 2) add better node-local socket pooling / reuse to reduce ephemeral sockets, 3) add alerting on node-local restarts and conntrack saturation.
Simon: I'll open infra ticket with kernel-rollback plan if canary doesn't hold across traffic. For now plan: rollback RDMA MTU clamp in us-west-2, roll conntrack bump to GPU pool, and adjust node-local DS to increase worker threads and disable per-query ephemeral UDP in next patch.
Jamie: created runbook snippet in the incident thread with commands and quick mitigation steps.
oncall: assigning oncall to monitor for 2 hours, will escalate if retry_rate > 15% again. :thumbsup:
